Subject: Mid-quarter health check: OKR realignment & resource asks for QBR

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse and asks ahead of the QBR readout next week. Overall signal: progress on platform throughput and Hosted API adoption is good, but two pockets are trending behind target and need immediate prioritization to avoid a low confidence QBR narrative. High-level items below, followed by specific requests.

Top-level status (concise)
- Platform reliability OKR (Reduce client-visible error rate to <=0.5%): GREEN for Hosted, AMBER for Dedicated.
- Cost-per-token OKR (10% reduction vs. baseline): AMBER overall; batching gains offset by elevated infrequent long-sequence runs.
- Latency P99 OKR (target -20%): RED on multi-tenant pools due to kernel regression on v2.3 runtime.

Root causes we surfaced
- Kernel rollout: a backend perf regression slipped past internal perf gates in the v2.3 compile path for sparse attention patterns. We need a hotfix and a coordinated rollback fallback path for Dedicated capacity.
- Workload mix: a small set (~12 clients) with high-length bursts are inflating cost and P99 for multi-tenant pools. We should have targeted throttles/caps and reroute policies ready to propose.
- Resourcing: Reconciling on-call and project bandwidth for the next 10 business days is the gating item for any near-term mitigation.

Requests (actionable)
1) Karthik — can your infra team commit a 48-hour hotfix window for the kernel path (identify engineer leads and on-call backup)? We need an ETA by EOD today to assess rollback vs. patch tradeoffs.
2) Vanessa — CS/Account leads: help me prioritize the client list for targeted routing (I propose the top 12 by traffic + 3 strategic accounts). Need confirmation by tomorrow noon so we can prepare customer comms.
3) Naomi — Product: please scope a reduced OKR target for latency that we can present at QBR (proposal: split out Dedicated vs. Multi-tenant targets and mark multi-tenant as mitigated-but-still-risk). Can you circulate a 1-slide proposal?

Attachments: I put a first-pass QBR readout and a resourcing workbook in the Drive link and attached the draft PDF for quicker read.

My suggested framing for QBR: be honest about the kernel regression, show an immediate mitigation plan (hotfix + routing + temporary throttle), and then surface the ask for 2 WEs of dedicated infra lead time to implement robust fallback routing + expanded perf gates.

If we all align on the approach now we can avoid an escalation and keep exec ask limited to resourcing (rather than a product-level scope rollback).

Thanks —
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Platform Strategy
Redwood Inference
